Jinja autoescaping prevents basic XSS; |safe must not be applied to uncontrolled input; escaping doesn't cover every context (attributes, URLs, <script> blocks) — correctly caveated -- confirmed accurate and appropriately scoped (does not overclaim autoescaping as a universal XSS fix)

CSRF explained correctly (browser auto-attaches cookies to cross-site requests); explicitly notes the chapter's project has no login so CSRF risk is 'limited', while still stating that state-changing requests relying on auto-sent cookies elsewhere need explicit CSRF protection -- confirmed reasonably honest framing given the actual project has zero CSRF tokens on its three POST routes (/dobavit, /vypolnit/<id>, /udalit/<id>) — not flagged as a defect since the text does not claim the project is CSRF-safe, only that risk is bounded by the absence of auth

Passwords must be hashed via a dedicated library, never stored plaintext or home-rolled; project explicitly stores no passwords at all -- confirmed accurate, consistent with 22.30's explicit no-auth scope decision

SECRET_KEY / DB passwords / API keys should not be committed to source, deferred to env-var handling in 22.34 -- confirmed accurate and consistent with the actual todo-app/app.py os.environ.get(...) pattern
